fields.text: Write 1 to return every GCLK register to its power-reset state, except generic clocks and their generators locked by PCHCTRLm.WRTLOCK = 1; writing 0 does nothing. The reset is synchronized, so it takes time; CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when it is done.

fields.name: SWRST

registers.name: GENCTRLn
registers.title: Generator Control
notes: One register per generic clock generator n, n = 0..8.

fields.name: DIV
fields.text: Division value for the generator, read according to DIVSEL. Generators 0 and 2 to 8 use 8 bits (DIV[7:0]), generator 1 uses 16 bits (DIV[15:0]); bits written beyond that are ignored.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Keeps the generator running in standby while it drives its GCLK_IO pin. Does nothing when GENCTRLn.OE is 0; the generator then runs only when a peripheral asks for its clock.

values.text: Generator stops in standby; the GCLK_IO level follows GENCTRL.OOV.
Generator keeps running in standby and keeps driving GCLK_IO.

fields.name: DIVSEL
fields.text: Chooses how DIV turns into the division of the generator's source clock. For no division, DIVSEL must be 0 with GENCTRLn.DIV at 0 or 1.

fields.name: OE
fields.text: Drives the generator clock out on its GCLK_IO pin, provided GCLK_IO is not chosen as the generator's source in GENCTRLn.SRC.

values.text: GCLK_IO carries the generator clock, unless GCLK_IO is the source chosen in GENCTRLn.SRC.

fields.name: OOV
fields.text: Level driven on GCLK_IO while the generator is off or OE is 0, provided GCLK_IO is not chosen as the generator's source in GENCTRLn.SRC.

values.text: GCLK_IO low while the generator is off or OE is 0.
GCLK_IO high while the generator is off or OE is 0.

fields.name: IDC
fields.text: Evens the generator output's duty cycle to 50/50 when the division factor is odd.

values.text: Duty cycle not evened for odd division factors.

fields.name: GENEN
fields.text: Turns the generator on or off.

fields.name: SRC
fields.text: Clock source of the generator. A power reset sets GENCTRL0 to 0x00000106 and the others to 0x00000000. A user reset does the same, except a generator feeding a locked peripheral channel (PCHCTRLm.WRTLOCK = 1) keeps its GENCTRL.

registers.name: PCHCTRLm
registers.title: Peripheral Channel Control
notes: One register per peripheral channel m, m = 0..34. Channel m clocks: 0 GCLK_DFLL48M_REF (DFLL48M reference), 1 GCLK_DPLL (FDPLL96M reference input), 2 GCLK_DPLL_32K (32 kHz clock for the FDPLL96M lock timer), 3 GCLK_EIC, 4 GCLK_USB, 5-16 GCLK_EVSYS_CHANNEL_0 to _11, 17 GCLK_SERCOM[0,1,2,3,4]_SLOW, 18-22 GCLK_SERCOM0_CORE to SERCOM4_CORE, 23 GCLK_SERCOM5_SLOW, 24 GCLK_SERCOM5_CORE, 25 GCLK_TCC0 and GCLK_TCC1, 26 GCLK_TCC2, 27 GCLK_TC0 and GCLK_TC1, 28 GCLK_TC2 and GCLK_TC3, 29 GCLK_TC4, 30 GCLK_ADC, 31 GCLK_AC, 32 GCLK_DAC, 33 GCLK_PTC, 34 GCLK_CCL.

fields.name: WRTLOCK
fields.text: Once set to 1, further writes to PCHCTRLm are dropped and the GENCTRLn of the generator chosen in PCHCTRLm.GEN is locked too; only a power reset unlocks them. Generator 0 cannot be locked.

values.text: Channel register and its generator register unlocked.
Channel register and its generator register locked.

fields.name: CHEN
fields.text: Turns the peripheral channel on or off.

fields.name: GEN
fields.text: Picks which generic clock generator feeds this peripheral channel. A power reset clears every PCHCTRLm to 0x0; a user reset clears a PCHCTRLm only when its WRTLOCK is 0, and leaves it unchanged when WRTLOCK is 1.

fields.name: CKRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Clock Ready interrupt and drop its request; a 0 does nothing.

fields.text: Prescaler ratio taking the main clock down to the CPU clock domain. Keep FCPU at or above FLP (LPDIV not below CPUDIV) and every domain within its maximum frequency.

fields.name: LPDIV

RTC keeps running while the CPU is halted by the debugger.

fields.name: CLOCKSYNC
fields.text: CLOCK Read Sync Enable Synchronization Busy status.

values.text: A write to CTRLA.CLOCKSYNC has finished synchronizing.
A write to CTRLA.CLOCKSYNC is still synchronizing.

fields.name: MASK0
fields.text: Mask 0 Synchronization Busy status.

values.text: A write to MASK0 has finished synchronizing.
A write to MASK0 is still synchronizing.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Alarm 0 Synchronization Busy status.

values.text: A write to ALARM0 has finished synchronizing.
A write to ALARM0 is still synchronizing.

fields.name: CLOCK
fields.text: Clock Register Synchronization Busy status.

values.text: A read or write of CLOCK has finished synchronizing.
A read or write of CLOCK is still synchronizing.

fields.name: FREQCORR
fields.text: Frequency Correction Synchronization Busy status.

values.text: A read or write of FREQCORR has finished synchronizing.
A read or write of FREQCORR is still synchronizing.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Enable Synchronization Busy status.

values.text: A read or write of CTRLA.ENABLE has finished synchronizing.
A read or write of CTRLA.ENABLE is still synchronizing.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Software Reset Synchronization Busy status.

values.text: A read or write of CTRLA.SWRST has finished synchronizing.
A read or write of CTRLA.SWRST is still synchronizing.

fields.name: SIGN
fields.text: Correction Sign.

values.text: Positive correction: the frequency goes down.
Negative correction: the frequency goes up.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: How much correction is applied to the RTC prescaler.

values.text: No correction; the RTC frequency is left as it is.
The RTC frequency is corrected by this amount.

registers.name: CLOCK
registers.title: Clock Value in Clock/Calendar mode (CTRLA.MODE = 2)
notes: Write CTRLA.CLOCKSYNC = 1 before any read of CLOCK, so reads are synchronized.
Writes are synchronized: SYNCBUSY.CLOCK shows when a write has finished.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Years counted from a reference year that software chooses; a year with YEAR[1:0] = 0 counts as a leap year.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Month, 1 for January through 12 for December.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Day of the month, from 1 up to 28, 29, 30 or 31 as the month and year allow.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Hour: 0 to 23 when CTRLA.CLKREP = 0; when CTRLA.CLKREP = 1, HOUR[3:0] runs 1 to 12 and HOUR[4] is 0 for AM, 1 for PM.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Minute, 0 to 59.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Second, 0 to 59.

registers.name: ALARM
registers.title: Alarm Value in Clock/Calendar mode (CTRLA.MODE=2)
notes: ALARM is compared with CLOCK all the time, over the fields MASK.SEL picks. On a match, INTFLAG.ALARM0 is set one counter cycle later, and the counter is cleared when CTRLA.MATCHCLR is 1.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Alarm year; compared only when MASK.SEL is 6.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Alarm month; compared only when MASK.SEL is above 4.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Alarm day; compared only when MASK.SEL is above 3.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Alarm hour; compared only when MASK.SEL is above 2.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Alarm minute; compared only when MASK.SEL is above 1.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Alarm second; compared only when MASK.SEL is above 0.

fields.name: SEL
fields.text: Chooses which ALARM fields take part in the match.

values.name: MMDDHHMMSS
values.text: Seconds, minutes, hours, days and months.

values.name: YYMMDDHHMMSS
values.text: Seconds, minutes, hours, days, months and years.

fields.name: GP
fields.text: Free for any use the user chooses.

fields.name: LVLENx
fields.text: Bit x lets requests at priority level x into the arbiter when set; cleared, those requests are ignored. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: CRCENABLE
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the CRC calculation on; writing 0 turns it off once CRCSTATUS.CRCBUSY is clear. Reads 0 while the CRC is off.

fields.name: DMAENABLE
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the DMA module on, 0 turns it off. A 0 written mid-transfer takes effect only after the internal transfer buffer drains (the current burst finishes) and the transfer is aborted. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 while both DMAENABLE and CRCENABLE are 0 returns every DMAC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value; with either one set the request is dropped and an access error results. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CRCSRC
fields.text: Picks where the CRC input comes from. Locked, as shown by CRCBUSY, until the CRC finishes or the CRC module is turned off, so it cannot change mid-calculation. With a DMA channel as source, that source signals when the CRC is complete.

fields.name: CRCPOLY
fields.text: Chooses the CRC polynomial.

fields.name: CRCBEATSIZE
fields.text: Width of each bus access when the CRC is fed through the I/O interface.

fields.name: CRCDATAIN
fields.text: Data word to run through the CRC; the new checksum is available CRCBEAT+1 clock cycles after a write here.

fields.name: CRCCHKSUM
fields.text: The computed CRC, 16 or 32 bits; with CRC-16 the upper 16 bits read 0. Resets to 0; a direct write, allowed only while the CRC module is off, can set every bit to 1. With CRC-32 and CRCSTATUS.CRCBUSY clear, it reads back bit-reversed (bit 31 swapped with bit 0, and so on) and complemented; with CRC-16, or while CRCBUSY is set, it reads the raw value.

fields.name: CRCZERO
fields.text: Set when a CRC calculation ends with a checksum of zero; cleared when a new CRC source is chosen. For CRC-32 with the checksum appended little-endian, the final value is 0x2144DF1C rather than zero; it is zero if the checksum was complemented before being appended.

fields.name: CRCBUSY
fields.text: Set once a source is chosen and held while that source uses the CRC. With the I/O interface it is cleared by writing 1. With a DMA channel it follows that channel's enable and software cannot clear it.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Decides whether the DMAC keeps running while an external debugger halts the CPU. A software reset leaves it unchanged.

fields.name: DQOS
fields.text: SRAM access priority for DMA data transfers.

fields.name: FQOS
fields.text: SRAM access priority for DMA descriptor fetches.

fields.name: WRBQOS
fields.text: SRAM access priority for DMA write-backs.

fields.name: SWTRIGn
fields.text: Writing 1 to bit n triggers channel n by software when its CHSTATUS.PEND is 0; PEND then goes to 1 and the bit stays 0. If PEND is already 1 the bit is set instead, and it clears when PEND sets. Writing 0, or writing 1 again, clears it.

fields.name: RRLVLEN3
fields.text: Selects the arbitration scheme for channels at priority level 3.

fields.name: LVLPRI3
fields.text: With round-robin on (RRLVLEN3=1), holds the number of the last level-3 channel granted access. With static arbitration a non-zero value has no effect on priority. Not cleared when round-robin is turned off.

fields.name: RRLVLEN2
fields.text: Selects the arbitration scheme for channels at priority level 2.

fields.name: LVLPRI2
fields.text: With round-robin on (RRLVLEN2=1), holds the number of the last level-2 channel granted access. With static arbitration a non-zero value has no effect on priority. Not cleared when round-robin is turned off.

fields.name: RRLVLEN1
fields.text: Arbitration for channels at priority level 1.

fields.name: LVLPRI1
fields.text: With round-robin on (RRLVLEN1=1), holds the number of the last level-1 channel granted access. With static arbitration a non-zero value has no effect on priority. Not cleared when round-robin is turned off.

fields.name: RRLVLEN0
fields.text: Arbitration for channels at priority level 0.

fields.name: LVLPRI0
fields.text: With round-robin on (RRLVLEN0=1), holds the number of the last level-0 channel granted access. With static arbitration a non-zero value has no effect on priority. Not cleared when round-robin is turned off.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID is pending.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID is busy.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has fetched an invalid descriptor.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has a Suspend interrupt waiting; writing 1 clears that channel's Suspend flag, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has a Transfer Complete interrupt waiting; writing 1 clears that channel's Transfer Complete flag, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has a Transfer Error interrupt waiting; writing 1 clears that channel's Transfer Error flag, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Lowest-numbered channel with an interrupt waiting, valid while SUSP, TCMPL or TERR is set; reads 0 when none is waiting. Updates when a lower channel gets an interrupt or the current one's sources are cleared. Writing it gives indirect access to that channel's interrupt flags.

fields.name: CHINTn
fields.text: Bit n is 1 while channel n has an interrupt request; it clears when that channel's interrupts are disabled or their sources cleared.

fields.name: BUSYCHn
fields.text: Bit n goes to 1 when channel n starts a transfer and back to 0 when its trigger action completes, a bus error hits it, or it is disabled.

fields.name: PENDCH
fields.text: Bit n is 1 while channel n has a transfer pending; it clears when the trigger action (CHCTRLB.TRIGACT) starts, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: Remaining 16-bit block transfer count of the transfer in progress, kept in the active channel and written back to that channel's write-back entry when another channel is granted. Valid only while ABUSY is 1.

fields.name: ABUSY
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the next descriptor's transfer count is read from write-back memory and to 0 when the active count is written back there.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Number of the channel now held in the active channel registers; updated on every new grant by the arbiter.

fields.name: LVLEXx
fields.text: Bit x reads 1 while some level-x channel trigger request is pending or running, and 0 otherwise.

fields.name: BASEADDR
fields.text: Start address of the descriptor memory section; must be 64-bit aligned.

fields.name: WRBADDR
fields.text: Start address of the write-back memory section; must be 64-bit aligned.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Channel that the CH* registers act on; write it before any access to a channel register.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Keeps the channel running in standby mode. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the channel on. A 0 written mid-transfer takes effect only after the internal transfer buffer drains (the current burst finishes) and the transfer is aborted. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns the channel registers to their reset values; accepted only while ENABLE=0 and ignored otherwise. Clears itself when the reset is done. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Software command to the channel. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: TRIGACT
fields.text: What one trigger starts.

fields.name: TRIGSRC
fields.text: Peripheral trigger that starts the channel's transfers; what each trigger does is set by TRIGACT.

fields.name: LVL
fields.text: Channel arbitration level: 0x0 to 0x3 select priority level 0 to 3 (LVL0 to LVL3); a higher level wins over a lower one. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: EVOE
fields.text: Turns on the channel's event output; an event is produced for each condition chosen by the descriptor's BTCTRL.EVOSEL. Present only on the lowest-numbered channels.

fields.name: EVIE
fields.text: Turns on the channel's event input. Present only on the lowest-numbered channels.

values.text: Each incoming event runs the event action.

fields.name: EVACT
fields.text: Action taken on an incoming event, only when EVIE is set. Present only on the lowest-numbered channels.

values.name: TRIG
values.text: Normal transfer; conditional transfer on strobe trigger.

values.name: SSKIP
values.text: Skip the next block suspend action.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the Channel Suspend interrupt enable, turning it off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the Channel Transfer Complete interrupt enable, turning it off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Channel Transfer Complete interrupt off; with block action set to none, TCMPL is not set at the end of a block.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the Channel Transfer Error interrupt enable, turning it off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Channel Suspend interrupt enable, turning it on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Channel Transfer Complete interrupt enable, turning it on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Channel Transfer Error interrupt enable, turning it on; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHINTFLAG
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Set when a block with a suspend block action finishes, a software suspend command runs, a suspend event arrives, or an invalid descriptor is fetched. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Set when a block transfer finishes and its block action includes the interrupt. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Set on a bus error during a beat transfer or when an invalid descriptor is fetched. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Goes to 1 when an invalid descriptor is fetched; cleared by a software resume command.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the channel starts a transfer; cleared when the trigger action completes, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: Goes to 1 as soon as a transfer request reaches the channel; cleared when the trigger action starts, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

fields.name: STEPSIZE
fields.text: Address step size, applied to the source or the destination address as STEPSEL chooses.

values.name: X1
values.text: Next address = address + beat size in bytes × 1.

values.name: X2
values.text: Next address = address + beat size in bytes × 2.

values.name: X4
values.text: Next address = address + beat size in bytes × 4.

values.name: X8
values.text: Next address = address + beat size in bytes × 8.

values.name: X16
values.text: Next address = address + beat size in bytes × 16.

values.name: X32
values.text: Next address = address + beat size in bytes × 32.

values.name: X64
values.text: Next address = address + beat size in bytes × 64.

values.name: X128
values.text: Next address = address + beat size in bytes × 128.

fields.name: STEPSEL
fields.text: Chooses which address uses STEPSIZE.

fields.name: DSTINC
fields.text: Writing 1 makes the destination address advance, by 1 unless STEPSEL=0 brings STEPSIZE into play; writing 0 holds it fixed for the transfer.

fields.name: SRCINC
fields.text: Writing 1 makes the source address advance, by 1 unless STEPSEL=1 brings STEPSIZE into play; writing 0 holds it fixed for the transfer.

fields.name: BEATSIZE
fields.text: Size of one beat, the data moved in one bus access, for both reads and writes.

fields.name: BLOCKACT
fields.text: What the DMAC does when a block transfer ends.

values.name: NOACT
values.text: Disable the channel if this was the transaction's last block.

values.name: INT
values.text: Disable the channel if this was the last block, and raise the block interrupt.

values.name: BOTH
values.text: Suspend the channel and raise the block interrupt.

fields.name: EVOSEL
fields.text: When the channel produces an output event.

values.name: BLOCK
values.text: Strobe at the end of each block transfer.

values.name: BEAT
values.text: Strobe at the end of each beat transfer.

fields.name: VALID
fields.text: A 0 here in descriptor or write-back memory suspends the channel when that descriptor is fetched. Hardware clears it in write-back memory when the channel is aborted, an error occurs in the block, or the block finishes.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: 16-bit block transfer count, counted down by one per beat. The running count is written to the channel's write-back entry when the channel loses priority, is suspended, or is disabled (by completion, a transfer error, or software).

fields.name: SRCADDR
fields.text: Source address for the block. With BTCTRL.SRCINC=0 it is the address of the last beat. With SRCINC=1 it is the first beat's address plus BTCNT × (BEATSIZE+1), times 2^STEPSIZE when BTCTRL.STEPSEL=1; BTCNT is the initial beat count, BEATSIZE the bytes per beat, STEPSIZE the beats per increment.

fields.name: DSTADDR
fields.text: Destination address for the block. With BTCTRL.DSTINC=0 it is the address of the last beat. With DSTINC=1 it is the first beat's address plus BTCNT × (BEATSIZE+1), times 2^STEPSIZE when BTCTRL.STEPSEL=0; BTCNT is the initial beat count, BEATSIZE the bytes per beat, STEPSIZE the beats per increment.

fields.name: DESCADDR
fields.text: LP SRAM address of the next descriptor, 128-bit aligned. A value of 0x00000000 ends the transaction when the DMAC goes to load the next descriptor.

fields.name: CKSEL
fields.text: Clock for the EIC: GCLK_EIC when filtering needs more than 32 kHz, CLK_ULP32K when low power matters most. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the EIC on or off. The written value reads back at once, but the change completes after synchronization, while SYNCBUSY.ENABLE is 1. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every EIC register to its reset value and disables the EIC; it overrides any other write in the same access. It completes after synchronization, when SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear. Writing 0 does nothing. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: NMIASYNCH
fields.text: Runs NMI edge detection either in step with the EIC clock or without it.

fields.name: NMIFILTEN
fields.text: Non-maskable interrupt filter enable.

fields.name: NMISENSE
fields.text: Edge or level on which the NMI fires.

registers.name: NMIFLAG
registers.title: Non-Maskable Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: NMI
fields.text: Set when the NMI pin meets the NMISENSE condition, raising an interrupt request. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Enable synchronization busy.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Software reset synchronization busy.

fields.name: EXTINTEO
fields.text: Bit x turns on the event output for pin EXTINTx.

values.text: Event from EXTINTx whenever the pin meets its sense setting.

fields.name: EXTINT
fields.text: Bit x is the interrupt enable for pin EXTINTx; writing 1 clears it, turning that interrupt off. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINT
fields.text: Bit x is the interrupt enable for pin EXTINTx; writing 1 sets it, turning that interrupt on. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINT
fields.text: Bit x is set when pin EXTINTx meets its sense setting, and requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.EXTINT[x] is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ASYNCH
fields.text: Bit x runs edge detection for pin EXTINTx asynchronously.

fields.name: FILTEN7
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+7].

fields.name: SENSE7
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+7] raises its interrupt or event.

fields.name: FILTEN6
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+6].

fields.name: SENSE6
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+6] raises its interrupt or event.

fields.name: FILTEN5
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+5].

fields.name: SENSE5
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+5] raises its interrupt or event.

fields.name: FILTEN4
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+4].

fields.name: SENSE4
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+4] raises its interrupt or event.

fields.name: FILTEN3
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+3].

fields.name: SENSE3
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+3] raises its interrupt or event.

fields.name: FILTEN2
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+2].

fields.name: SENSE2
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+2] raises its interrupt or event.

fields.name: FILTEN1
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+1].

fields.name: SENSE1
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+1] raises its interrupt or event.

fields.name: FILTEN0
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+0].

fields.name: SENSE0
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+0] raises its interrupt or event.

fields.name: CMDEX
fields.text: Key field: writing 0xA5 here, in the same write as CMD, runs the command in CMD. With any other value the whole write is dropped and STATUS.PROGE is set; PROGE is also set when the previous command has not finished. INTFLAG.READY must be 1 when a command is given. An APB command arriving in the same cycle as an AHB access waits for the AHB access, and runs once both the AHB bus and the NVM block go idle. Bit 0 reads 1 until the command is given. ADDR.ADDR counts in 16-bit half-words.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Selects the NVM command run when the CMDEX key is written.

values.name: ER
values.text: Erases the NVM main-array row that ADDR points to.

values.name: WP
values.text: Writes the page buffer into the page that ADDR points to.

values.name: EAR
values.text: Erases the auxiliary row that ADDR points to; allowed only on the User Configuration Row and only while the security bit is clear.

values.name: WAP
values.text: Writes the page buffer into the auxiliary page that ADDR points to; allowed only on the User Configuration Row and only while the security bit is clear.

values.name: RWWEEER
values.text: Erases the RWWEE-array row that ADDR points to.

values.name: RWWEEWP
values.text: Writes the page buffer into the RWWEE-array page that ADDR points to.

values.name: LR
values.text: Locks the lock region holding the address in ADDR.

values.name: UR
values.text: Unlocks the lock region holding the address in ADDR.

values.name: SPRM
values.text: Puts the NVM into power reduction mode.

values.name: CPRM
values.text: Takes the NVM out of power reduction mode.

values.name: SSB
values.text: Sets the security bit, by writing 0x00 into the first byte of the lockbit row.

fields.name: CACHEDIS
fields.text: Turns the cache on or off for the NVM and the RWW EEPROM; both share one cache.

fields.name: READMODE
fields.text: NVMCTRL read mode.

values.name: NO_MISS_PENALTY
values.text: No wait states added on a cache miss; highest system performance.

values.name: LOW_POWER
values.text: Lower cache-system power, with one wait state added on every cache miss; the CPU stalls on misses, which can lengthen run time.

values.name: DETERMINISTIC
values.text: Hits and misses take the same time, set by the programmed flash wait states; for code needing deterministic timing.

fields.name: SLEEPPRM
fields.text: Chooses how the NVM uses power reduction mode in sleep.

values.name: WAKEUPACCESS
values.text: NVM enters low-power mode on sleep and leaves it at the first access.

values.name: WAKEUPINSTANT
values.text: NVM enters low-power mode on sleep and leaves it when sleep ends.

fields.name: MANW
fields.text: Manual write; resets to 1.

values.text: A write to the last word of the page buffer starts a write of the page addressed by the last write, for memory and auxiliary rows alike.
Writes happen only by commands through CTRLA.CMD.

fields.name: RWS
fields.text: Number of NVM read wait states, 0 to 15, one per count; resets to 0. Software may change it to suit the NVM access time and system clock.

fields.name: RWWEEP
fields.text: How many pages the RWW EEPROM emulation space holds.

fields.name: PSZ
fields.text: Page size; not every device in the families offers every page size.

fields.name: NVMP
fields.text: Number of pages in the NVM main space.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Disables interrupts with no read-modify-write; changes also show in INTENSET.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the ERROR interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads back the ERROR interrupt enable.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the READY interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads back the READY interrupt enable.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Enables interrupts with no read-modify-write; changes also show in INTENCLR.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the ERROR interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads back the ERROR interrupt enable.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the READY interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads back the READY interrupt enable.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Set by an NVME, LOCKE or PROGE error; write 1 to clear.

values.text: No error since the flag was last cleared.
One or more errors since the flag was last cleared.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: NVM ready.

values.text: The controller is busy with a program or erase.
The controller can take a new command.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Security bit status.

fields.name: NVME
fields.text: NVM error; write 1 to clear.

values.text: The NVM controller has reported no program or erase error since this bit was last cleared.
The NVM controller has reported one or more errors since this bit was last cleared.

fields.name: LOCKE
fields.text: Lock error; write 1 to clear.

values.text: No locked region has been programmed since this bit was last cleared.
A locked region has been programmed at least once since this bit was last cleared.

fields.name: PROGE
fields.text: Programming error; write 1 to clear.

values.text: Since the last clear of this bit, no invalid command or wrong key has reached the command register.
Since the last clear of this bit, an invalid command, a wrong key, or both, have reached the command register.

fields.name: LOAD
fields.text: Set as soon as one or more words are loaded into the page buffer; stays set until a page is written or a PBCLR command empties the buffer. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: PRM
fields.text: Shows whether the NVM is in power reduction mode. It enters it by command or on sleep, per SLEEPPRM; it leaves it on an AHB access to the NVM, by the SPRM/CPRM commands, or on leaving sleep, per SLEEPPRM.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Half-word offset from the start of the NVM section that a CMDEX command acts on; the address used is the section start + 2*ADDR. Writing the page buffer also updates it. Erasing the third flash row (0x00000200 to 0x000002FF), for instance, takes any ADDR from 0x100 to 0x17F.

fields.name: LOCK
fields.text: One lock bit per region, changed only through CMD commands; after erase all regions are unlocked (0xFFFF).

registers.name: DIR
registers.title: Data Direction
notes: Sets each pin as input or output; DIRCLR, DIRSET and DIRTGL change it with no read-modify-write.
Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Direction of each I/O pin in the PORT group.

registers.name: DIRCLR
registers.title: Data Direction Clear
notes: Makes pins inputs with no read-modify-write; changes also show in DIR, DIRTGL and DIRSET.
Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: DIRCLR
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the matching DIR bit, making the pin an input; 0 does nothing.

registers.name: DIRSET
registers.title: Data Direction Set
notes: Makes pins outputs with no read-modify-write; changes also show in DIR, DIRTGL and DIRCLR.

fields.name: DIRSET
fields.text: Write 1 to set the matching DIR bit, making the pin an output; 0 does nothing.

registers.name: DIRTGL
registers.title: Data Direction Toggle
notes: Reverses pin directions with no read-modify-write; changes also show in DIR, DIRSET and DIRCLR.
Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: DIRTGL
fields.text: Write 1 to toggle the matching DIR bit, reversing the pin's direction; 0 does nothing.

registers.name: OUT
registers.title: Data Output Value
notes: Output level of each pin; OUTCLR, OUTSET and OUTTGL change it with no read-modify-write.
Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: OUT
fields.text: Output level for pins set as outputs in DIR; for pins set as inputs with PINCFG.PULLEN on, it picks the pull direction.

values.text: Output low, or input pulled down.
Output high, or input pulled up.

registers.name: OUTCLR
registers.title: Data Output Value Clear
notes: Drives outputs low with no read-modify-write; changes also show in OUT, OUTTGL and OUTSET.
Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: OUTCLR
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the matching OUT bit: outputs go low, and inputs with PINCFG.PULLEN on get the pull-down; 0 does nothing.

values.text: Output low, or input pulled down.

registers.name: OUTSET
registers.title: Data Output Value Set
notes: Drives outputs high with no read-modify-write; changes also show in OUT, OUTTGL and OUTCLR.
Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: OUTSET
fields.text: Write 1 to set the matching OUT bit: outputs go high, and inputs with pull enabled (PULLEN) get the pull-up; 0 does nothing.

values.text: Output high, or input pulled up.

registers.name: OUTTGL
registers.title: Data Output Value Toggle
notes: Inverts output levels with no read-modify-write; changes also show in OUT, OUTSET and OUTCLR.
Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: OUTTGL
fields.text: Write 1 to toggle the matching OUT bit: outputs invert their level, and inputs with pull enabled (PULLEN) swap pull direction; 0 does nothing.

registers.name: IN
registers.title: Data Input Value
notes: Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: IN
fields.text: Pin level as read by the input sampler: 0 for low, 1 for high.

registers.name: CTRL
registers.title: Control
notes: Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: SAMPLING
fields.text: Input sampling mode for pins set as inputs in DIR. Samplers switch on and off in groups of eight pins, so one pin asking for continuous sampling makes all eight in its byte sample continuously.

registers.name: WRCONFIG
registers.title: Write Configuration
notes: Write-only: gives many pins the same configuration and/or multiplexing at once. 8- and 16-bit writes do nothing; reads return 0.
Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: HWSEL
fields.text: Picks which half of the 32-pin PORT group the atomic write configures; reads 0.

fields.name: WRPINCFG
fields.text: Write 1 to load the written DRVSTR, PULLEN, INEN, PMUXEN and PINMASK values into PINCFGy of every pin picked by PINMASK and HWSEL; 0 does nothing. Reads 0.

fields.name: WRPMUX
fields.text: Write 1 to load the written PMUX value into PMUXn of every pin picked by PINMASK and HWSEL; 0 does nothing. Reads 0.

fields.name: PMUX
fields.text: Value put in PMUXn of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPMUX is set; reads 0.

fields.name: DRVSTR
fields.text: Value put in PINCFGy.DRVSTR of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is set; reads 0.

fields.name: PULLEN
fields.text: Value put in PINCFGy.PULLEN of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is set; reads 0.

fields.name: INEN
fields.text: Value put in PINCFGy.INEN of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is set; reads 0.

fields.name: PMUXEN
fields.text: Value put in PINCFGy.PMUXEN of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is set; reads 0.

fields.name: PINMASK
fields.text: Picks the pins to configure in the half-word chosen by HWSEL; reads 0.

registers.name: EVCTRL
registers.title: Event Input Control
notes: Each PORT group has up to four event input pins, one per byte of this register.
Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: PORTEI3
fields.text: Enables event input 3.

values.text: Incoming events do not trigger EVACT3.

fields.name: EVACT3
fields.text: Action the PORT takes on an event at input 3: OUT (0x0) sets the pin's output register to the event level, SET (0x1) sets it, CLR (0x2) clears it, TGL (0x3) toggles it.

values.name: OUT
values.text: Pin's output register follows the event level.

values.name: SET
values.text: Pin's output register is set on each event.

values.name: CLR
values.text: Pin's output register is cleared on each event.

values.name: TGL
values.text: Pin's output register toggles on each event.

fields.name: PID3
fields.text: Picks the I/O pin that event input 3 acts on: PIN0 (0x0) to PIN31 (0x1F).

fields.name: PORTEI2
fields.text: Enables event input 2.

values.text: Incoming events do not trigger EVACT2.

fields.name: EVACT2
fields.text: Action the PORT takes on an event at input 2: OUT (0x0) sets the pin's output register to the event level, SET (0x1) sets it, CLR (0x2) clears it, TGL (0x3) toggles it.

values.name: OUT
values.text: Pin's output register follows the event level.

values.name: SET
values.text: Pin's output register is set on each event.

values.name: CLR
values.text: Pin's output register is cleared on each event.

values.name: TGL
values.text: Pin's output register toggles on each event.

fields.name: PID2
fields.text: Picks the I/O pin that event input 2 acts on: PIN0 (0x0) to PIN31 (0x1F).

fields.name: PORTEI1
fields.text: Enables event input 1.

values.text: Incoming events do not trigger EVACT1.

fields.name: EVACT1
fields.text: Action the PORT takes on an event at input 1: OUT (0x0) sets the pin's output register to the event level, SET (0x1) sets it, CLR (0x2) clears it, TGL (0x3) toggles it.

values.name: OUT
values.text: Pin's output register follows the event level.

values.name: SET
values.text: Pin's output register is set on each event.

values.name: CLR
values.text: Pin's output register is cleared on each event.

values.name: TGL
values.text: Pin's output register toggles on each event.

fields.name: PID1
fields.text: Picks the I/O pin that event input 1 acts on: PIN0 (0x0) to PIN31 (0x1F).

fields.name: PORTEI0
fields.text: Enables event input 0.

values.text: Incoming events do not trigger EVACT0.

fields.name: EVACT0
fields.text: Action the PORT takes on an event at input 0: OUT (0x0) sets the pin's output register to the event level, SET (0x1) sets it, CLR (0x2) clears it, TGL (0x3) toggles it.

values.name: OUT
values.text: Pin's output register follows the event level.

values.name: SET
values.text: Pin's output register is set on each event.

values.name: CLR
values.text: Pin's output register is cleared on each event.

values.name: TGL
values.text: Pin's output register toggles on each event.

fields.name: PID0
fields.text: Picks the I/O pin that event input 0 acts on: PIN0 (0x0) to PIN31 (0x1F).

registers.name: PMUX
registers.title: Peripheral Multiplexing n
notes: Up to 16 PMUXn per group, one per pair of neighbouring pins; n is the pair number.
Pins come in PORT groups of up to 32: group 0 is PA, group 1 PB, and so on, each with its own registers 0x80 apart (DIR at 0x00 for PA, 0x80 for PB).

fields.name: PMUXO
fields.text: Peripheral function of the odd pin (2*n + 1) of the pair, used when that pin's PINCFGy.PMUXEN is 1; not every code may be valid. 0x0 to 0x8 pick functions A to I; 0x9 to 0xF are reserved.

fields.name: PMUXE
fields.text: Peripheral function of the even pin (2*n) of the pair, used when that pin's PINCFGy.PMUXEN is 1; not every code may be valid. 0x0 to 0x8 pick functions A to I; 0x9 to 0xF are reserved.

fields.name: DRVSTR
fields.text: Drive strength of a pin set as an output.

fields.name: PULLEN
fields.text: Turns on the internal pull-up or pull-down of a pin set as an input.

values.text: No pull; the input floats at high impedance.
Pull on; the input sits at a set level when nothing drives it.

fields.name: INEN
fields.text: Input buffer of the pin, whether input or output; with 0 the buffer is fully off and the pin's level cannot be read back.

values.text: Buffer off; the pin is not sampled.
Buffer on; the pin is sampled when needed.

fields.name: PMUXEN
fields.text: Hands the pin's direction and output level to the peripheral chosen in PMUXn. At 0 the PORT drives them from DIR and OUT and PMUXn is ignored; at 1 the chosen peripheral does, and IN still shows the pin if PINCFGn.INEN is set.

values.text: The peripheral chosen in PMUXn controls the pin.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every EVSYS register to its reset state; 0 does nothing. It wins over any other write in the same access, which is dropped. Disabling event generators first is recommended.

registers.name: CHSTATUS
registers.title: Channel Status
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x000000FF.

fields.name: CHBUSYn
fields.text: One bit per channel: 1 while an event on the channel has not yet been handled by all its users, 0 when the channel is idle.

fields.name: USRRDYn
fields.text: One bit per channel: 1 when every user on the channel is ready for events, 0 when any one is not.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Disables interrupts with no read-modify-write; changes also show in INTENSET.

fields.name: EVDn
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the channel's Event Detected interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVRn
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the channel's Overrun interrupt; 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Enables interrupts with no read-modify-write; changes also show in INTENCLR.

fields.name: EVDn
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the channel's Event Detected interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVRn
fields.text: Write 1 to set the channel's Overrun interrupt enable bit; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EVDn
fields.text: Goes to 1 at the CLK_EVSYS_APB edge that follows an event moving through the channel, raising an interrupt if EVDn is enabled; stays 0 on the asynchronous path. Write 1 to clear; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVRn
fields.text: Goes to 1 at the CLK_EVSYS_APB edge that follows an event moving through the channel, raising an interrupt if OVRn is enabled; stays 0 on the asynchronous path. Write 1 to clear; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CHANNELn
fields.text: Write 1 to fire a software event on channel n; 0 does nothing. Reads 0.

registers.name: CHANNELn
registers.title: Channel
notes: Configures channel n; written as one 32-bit write holding all the settings.

fields.name: ONDEMAND
fields.text: Decides when the channel's generic clock is requested.

values.text: Clock always running while the channel is configured and its clock source is on.
Clock requested only while an event is being handled.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Channel behaviour in standby sleep.

values.text: Channel keeps running in standby, subject to CHANNEL.ONDEMAND.

fields.name: EDGSEL
fields.text: Edge the channel detects; must be 0 on the asynchronous path.

values.name: NO_EVT_OUTPUT
values.text: No event output on the resynchronized or synchronous path.

values.name: RISING_EDGE
values.text: Rising edge of the generator signal.

values.name: FALLING_EDGE
values.text: Falling edge of the generator signal.

values.name: BOTH_EDGES
values.text: Both edges of the generator signal.

fields.name: PATH
fields.text: Path the channel uses; the channel's source may limit the choice.

fields.name: EVGEN
fields.text: Selects which event generator feeds this channel.

rows: Compare 0 in modes 0 and 1, Alarm 0 in mode 2.

fields.name: CHANNEL
fields.text: Channel feeding this event user: write m+1 to pick channel m. Users 0-3 PORT EV0-3, 4-11 DMAC CH0-7, 12-17 TCC0 EV0/EV1/MC0-3, 18-21 TCC1 EV0/EV1/MC0/MC1, 22-25 TCC2 EV0/EV1/MC0/MC1, 26-30 TC0-TC4, 31 ADC START, 32 ADC SYNC, 33-34 AC COMP0/1, 35-36 DAC START0/1, 37 PTC STCONV, 38-41 CCL LUTIN0-3, 43 MTB START, 44 MTB STOP; 42 and above 44 reserved. DMAC users take synchronous and resynchronized paths only; the rest take all three.

peripherals.name: SERCOM USART
peripherals.title: SERCOM Universal Synchronous and Asynchronous Receiver and Transmitter

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Picks which end of a character leaves the data register first. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: In synchronous mode, picks which XCK edge changes TxD and which edge samples RxD. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CMODE
fields.text: Picks asynchronous or synchronous operation. Not synchronized.

fields.name: FORM
fields.text: Picks the frame format. Not synchronized.

values.text: Auto-baud (break detection and auto-baud), parity on.

fields.name: SAMPA
fields.text: Sets the sample adjustment. Not synchronized.

fields.name: RXPO
fields.text: Picks the SERCOM pad that receives data (RxD). Not synchronized.

fields.name: TXPO
fields.text: Picks the pads used for TxD and XCK. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SAMPR
fields.text: Picks the oversampling rate and the baud generation method. Not synchronized.

fields.name: IBON
fields.text: Picks when STATUS.BUFOVF goes high after a buffer overflow.

values.text: At the overflow's place in the data stream.
As soon as the overflow happens.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets what the USART does in standby sleep, with external and internal clock. Not synchronized.

rows: When the transfer in progress ends, the external clock is disconnected; all reception is dropped.
When the transfer in progress ends, the generic clock stops; the Transfer Complete interrupt can wake the device.
Receive Complete interrupt wakes the device.
Generic clock runs in every sleep mode; any interrupt can wake the device.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Picks the SERCOM's USART mode. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the SERCOM on or off. The written value reads back at once while SYNCBUSY.ENABLE is set; the change takes effect after synchronization, when SYNCBUSY.ENABLE clears. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every SERCOM register except DBGCTRL to its reset state and disable the SERCOM; a 0 write does nothing. It overrides any other write in the same access. During the reset, register writes give an APB error and reads return reset values. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when the reset, delayed by synchronization, is done. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: Turns the receiver on or off. Writing 0 turns it off, empties the receive buffer and clears STATUS.FERR, PERR and BUFOVF. Writing 1 with the USART off sets the bit at once. With the USART on, a 1 write sets SYNCBUSY.CTRLB until the receiver is running, and the bit then reads 1. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Receiver off, or being turned on.
Receiver on, or turns on when the USART is enabled.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: Turns the transmitter on or off. Writing 0 turns it off only after transmissions under way and waiting have finished. Writing 1 with the USART off sets the bit at once. With the USART on, a 1 write sets SYNCBUSY.CTRLB until the transmitter is running, and the bit then reads 1. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Transmitter off, or being turned on.
Transmitter on, or turns on when the USART is enabled.

fields.name: PMODE
fields.text: Picks even or odd parity when CTRLA.FORM enables parity. The transmitter adds the parity bit to each frame; the receiver checks incoming parity and sets STATUS.PERR on a mismatch. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENC
fields.text: Picks the data encoding. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SFDE
fields.text: Lets a start bit on RxD wake the device through the start-of-frame detector. Not synchronized.

values.text: Start-of-frame detection on; RXC wakes the device from every sleep mode.
Start-of-frame detection on; RXS wakes the device from every sleep mode.
Start-of-frame detection on; RXC and RXS both wake the device from every sleep mode.

fields.name: COLDEN
fields.text: Turns collision detection on. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SBMODE
fields.text: Picks how many stop bits are sent. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CHSIZE
fields.text: Picks how many bits make up a character. Not synchronized.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Baud value. With arithmetic baud generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0]=0) these bits set the clock generation; with fractional generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0]=1) bits 15:13 are replaced by the fractional part FP[2:0].

fields.name: FP
fields.text: Fractional part of the baud value, used with fractional baud generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0]=1).

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Integer part of the baud value, used with fractional baud generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0]=1).

fields.name: RXPL
fields.text: With IrDA encoding (CTRLB.ENC=1), sets the shortest pulse the IrDA receiver accepts: PULSE >= (RXPL + 2) x SEper, SEper being the serial engine clock period.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Writing 1 to a bit here turns that interrupt off without a read-modify-write; the change shows in INTENSET as well.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Error interrupt enable and turn that interrupt off; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Receive Break interrupt enable and turn that interrupt off; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the CTS input change interrupt by clearing its enable bit; a 0 write does nothing.

values.text: Clear To Send Input Change interrupt off.
Clear To Send Input Change interrupt on.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Receive Start interrupt enable and turn that interrupt off; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Receive Complete interrupt enable and turn that interrupt off; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Transmit Complete interrupt enable and turn that interrupt off; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Data Register Empty interrupt enable and turn that interrupt off; a 0 write does nothing.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Writing 1 to a bit here turns that interrupt on without a read-modify-write; the change shows in INTENCLR as well.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Error interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Receive Break interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the CTS input change interrupt by setting its enable bit; a 0 write does nothing.

values.text: Clear To Send Input Change interrupt off.
Clear To Send Input Change interrupt on.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Receive Start interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Receive Complete interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Transmit Complete interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Data Register Empty interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Goes high on any error that has its own STATUS flag: COLL, ISF, BUFOVF, FERR or PERR. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Goes high when a break character arrives with auto-baud on (CTRLA.FORM). Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Goes high when the CTS pin changes. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Goes high when a start condition is seen on RxD with start-of-frame detection on (CTRLB.SFDE=1). Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: High while DATA holds unread data. Reading DATA or turning the receiver off clears it; writes do nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Goes high once the whole frame has left the transmit shift register and DATA holds nothing new. Writing 1, or writing new data to DATA, clears it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: High while DATA is empty and can take new data. Writing new data to DATA clears it; writes to the bit do nothing.

fields.name: COLL
fields.text: Goes high when collision detection is on (CTRLB.COLDEN) and a collision occurs. Writing 1, or turning the receiver off, clears it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: ISF
fields.text: Goes high when, in auto-baud format (CTRLA.FORM), the sync field received is not 0x55. Writing 1, or turning the receiver off, clears it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: CTS
fields.text: Shows the present level on the CTS pin while flow control is on (CTRLA.TXPO). Writes do nothing.

fields.name: BUFOVF
fields.text: Goes high on a receive buffer overflow: buffer full, a character waiting in the shift register and a new start bit seen. Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. Writing 1, or turning the receiver off, clears it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Goes high when the received character's first stop bit is 0. Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. Writing 1, or turning the receiver off, clears it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: PERR
fields.text: Goes high on a parity mismatch while parity checking is on (CTRLA.FORM 0x1 or 0x5). Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. Writing 1, or turning the receiver off, clears it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: CTRLB
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLB made with the SERCOM on is being synchronized. Writing CTRLB while this is set gives an APB error.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized. Writes to any register other than CTRLA.SWRST during that time are dropped and give an APB error.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized. Writes to any register during that time are dropped and give an APB error.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: A read gives the receive data register, a write loads the transmit data register. Read it only when INTFLAG.RXC is set, after reading STATUS for that character's errors; write it only when INTFLAG.DRE is set.

fields.name: DBGSTOP
fields.text: Picks whether the baud-rate generator stops while an external debugger halts the CPU.

values.text: Baud-rate generator keeps running during a debugger halt.
Baud-rate generator stops during a debugger halt.

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Picks which end of a character leaves the shift register first. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: With CPHA, sets the SPI transfer mode. Not synchronized.

values.text: SCK idles low; leading edge rising, trailing edge falling.
SCK idles high; leading edge falling, trailing edge rising.

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: With CPOL, sets the SPI transfer mode. Mode 0x0 (CPOL 0, CPHA 0): sample on rising leading edge, change on falling trailing edge. 0x1 (0,1): change on rising leading edge, sample on falling trailing edge. 0x2 (1,0): sample on falling leading edge, change on rising trailing edge. 0x3 (1,1): change on falling leading edge, sample on rising trailing edge. Not synchronized.

values.text: Sample on the leading SCK edge, change on the trailing edge.
Change on the leading SCK edge, sample on the trailing edge.

fields.name: FORM
fields.text: Picks the frame format in Client mode. With the address format, the first byte received is compared with the ADDR register.

fields.name: DIPO
fields.text: Picks the pad for data in (DI): MISO in Host mode, MOSI in Client mode. Not synchronized.

fields.name: DOPO
fields.text: Picks the pads for data out (DO) and SCK. In Client mode DOPO also places SS; in Host mode SS is set by the port configuration. DO is MOSI in Host mode and MISO in Client mode. Not synchronized.

fields.name: IBON
fields.text: Picks when STATUS.BUFOVF is set after a buffer overflow. Not synchronized.

values.text: At the overflow's place in the data stream.
As soon as the overflow happens.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets what the SPI does in standby sleep, in Client and Host mode. Not synchronized.

rows: Off; all reception is dropped, the transaction in progress included.
When the transaction in progress ends, the generic clock stops; any interrupt can wake the device.
The transaction in progress carries on; the Receive Complete interrupt wakes the device.
The generic clock keeps running in sleep modes; any interrupt can wake the device.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Selects SPI on the SERCOM; write 0x2 or 0x3. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the SERCOM on or off. The written value reads back at once while SYNCBUSY.ENABLE is set; the change takes effect after synchronization, when SYNCBUSY.ENABLE clears. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every SERCOM register except DBGCTRL to its reset state and disable the SERCOM; a 0 write does nothing. It overrides any other write in the same access. During the reset, register writes give an APB error and reads return reset values. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when the reset, delayed by synchronization, is done. fields.name: RXEN

Writing 1 with the SPI off sets the bit at once. With the SPI on, a 1 write sets SYNCBUSY.CTRLB until the receiver is running, and the bit then reads 1. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: ERROR

fields.name: SSL

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: High while the receive buffer holds unread data; with address matching on, the first byte of a transaction is the address. Reading DATA or turning the receiver off clears it; writes do nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: In Host mode, goes high once the data has been shifted out and DATA holds nothing new; in Client mode, when SS goes high. With address matching on, it is set only for a transaction that began with a matching address. Writing 1, or writing new data to DATA, clears it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: High while DATA is empty and can take new data to send. Writing new data to DATA clears it; writes to the bit do nothing.

fields.name: BUFOVF
fields.text: Goes high on a receive buffer overflow; the RxDATA in question then reads 0. Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. CTRLA.IBON governs overflow handling. Writing 1, or turning the receiver off, clears it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: CTRLB

fields.name: DATA

fields.name: ACKACT

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Writing a code starts a Client operation; the bits are strobes and read back as zero. What happens depends on INTFLAG.DRDY, INTFLAG.AMATCH and STATUS.DIR. Giving a command clears INTFLAG.DRDY, INTFLAG.AMATCH and INTFLAG.PREC. Not enable-protected.

After AMATCH: acknowledge action, then receive the next byte (DIR 0) or raise the Client data interrupt (DIR 1). After DRDY: acknowledge action, then receive the next byte (DIR 0) or read a byte and then receive ACK/NACK (DIR 1).

fields.name: DRDY

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Error interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Data Ready interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: AMATCH
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Address Match interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: PREC
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Stop Received interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Goes high on any error that has its own STATUS flag: LENERR, SEXTTOUT, LOWTOUT, COLL or BUSERR. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: Goes high when the Client finishes sending or receiving a byte. Hardware clears it on a write to DATA, a read of DATA with smart mode on, or a valid command written to CMD. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: AMATCH
fields.text: Goes high when the Client's address logic sees a valid address. Hardware clears it when CTRLB.CMD is written. Write 1 to clear it, which sends ACK or NACK as CTRLB.ACKACT says; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: PREC
fields.text: Goes high when a stop condition ends a transaction this Client is handling; a stop between the Host and another Client does not set it unless the PMBus group command is on (CTRLB.GCMD=1). Hardware clears it after a command on the next address match. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: LENERR
fields.text: Goes high when, with LENGTH.LENEN on, a STOP or repeated START comes before or after LENGTH.LEN bytes. Clears by itself when a new start is answered with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD=0x3) or INTFLAG.AMATCH clears. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Goes high when the Client sees a START followed by a Host Code. Clears by itself on STOP. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: SEXTTOUT
fields.text: Goes high on a Client SCL low extend time-out. Clears by itself when a new start is answered with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD=3) or INTFLAG.AMATCH clears. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: High while the Client stretches the clock by holding SCL low; set whenever INTFLAG.DRDY or INTFLAG.AMATCH goes high, and cleared along with that flag. Treat it as read-only.

fields.name: LOWTOUT
fields.text: Goes high on an SCL low time-out. Clears by itself when a new start is answered with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD=3) or INTFLAG.AMATCH clears. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: SR
fields.text: Says whether the address match that raised INTFLAG.AMATCH came after a start or a repeated start. Valid only while INTFLAG.AMATCH is 1.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Direction of the last address packet from the Host.

fields.name: RXNACK
fields.text: Says whether the Host acknowledged the last data packet sent.

fields.name: COLL
fields.text: Goes high when the Client could not drive a high data bit or NACK; it then releases SDA and SCL and waits for the next packet addressed to it. Meant for SMBus ARP; outside ARP a collision is a protocol violation, to be handled as a bus error. It raises no interrupt, so software checks it to confirm the data went out. Clears by itself when an address match is answered with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD=0x3) or INTFLAG.AMATCH clears. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

values.text: No collision on the last byte sent.
Collision on the last byte sent.

fields.name: BUSERR
fields.text: Goes high on an illegal bus condition, whoever owns the bus: a misplaced start, repeated start or stop (a start straight followed by a stop is one), or a time-out during a frame. Clears by itself when an address match is answered with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD=0x3) or INTFLAG.AMATCH clears. Write 1 to clear it; a 0 write does nothing.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized. Writes to any register other than CTRLA.SWRST during that time are dropped and give an APB error.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized. Writes to any register during that time are dropped and give an APB error.

fields.name: ADDRMASK
fields.text: A second match address, an address mask, or the low end of an address range, as CTRLB.AMODE selects.

fields.name: TENBITEN
fields.text: Turns on 10-bit address recognition.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: The Client's own address, compared with what the Host sends: ADDR[6:0] with 7-bit addressing, ADDR[9:0] with 10-bit (ADDR.TENBITEN=1). On a match, INTFLAG.AMATCH goes high and STATUS.DIR shows read or write.

fields.name: GENCEN
fields.text: Turns on recognition of the general call address, all zeros including the direction bit (Host write).

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Window onto the Host's transmit and receive data buffers. Reads and writes succeed only while the Client holds SCL low (STATUS.CLKHOLD set), except reading the last byte after a stop. Each access starts I2C bus activity that depends on CTRLB.ACKACT, CTRLB.SMEN and the access type. Outside smart mode, access needs no synchronization.

fields.name: LOWTOUT
fields.text: Turns on the SCL low time-out: when SCL stays low for 25-35 ms the Host lets go of its clock hold (if enabled), finishes the transaction and sends a stop condition on its own; INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB sets as usual and STATUS.LOWTOUT and STATUS.BUSERR are set. Not synchronized.

fields.name: INACTOUT
fields.text: Inactive bus time-out: when on and the bus stays inactive (SCL held low by a Host or Client) past the chosen period, the bus state logic goes to idle. Needed for SMBus, usable without it. The periods assume a 100 kHz baud rate. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SCLSM
fields.text: Chooses when SCL is stretched for software to act. Not synchronized.

values.text: SCL stretched before or after the ACK bit.
SCL stretched only after the ACK bit.

fields.name: SPEED
fields.text: Selects the bus speed. Not synchronized.

values.text: Standard-mode up to 100 kHz and Fast-mode up to 400 kHz.

fields.name: SEXTTOEN
fields.text: Turns on the Client SCL low extend time-out: when SCL is held low for more than 25 ms in total between the first START and a STOP, the Host lets go of its clock hold (if enabled), finishes the transaction and sends a STOP on its own; SB or MB sets as usual, CLKHOLD is released, and the MEXTTOUT and BUSERR status bits are set. Not synchronized.

fields.name: MEXTTOEN
fields.text: Turns on the Host SCL low extend time-out: when SCL is held low for more than 10 ms in total over any one stretch (START to first ACK, between ACKs, or last ACK to STOP), the Host lets go of its clock hold (if enabled), finishes the transaction and sends a STOP on its own; SB or MB sets as usual, CLKHOLD is released, and the MEXTTOUT and BUSERR status bits are set. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SDAHOLD
fields.text: How long SDA is held after the falling edge of SCL. Not synchronized.

fields.name: PINOUT
fields.text: Picks two-wire or four-wire pin use. Not synchronized.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Sets behaviour in standby sleep mode. Not synchronized.

values.text: GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE is off and the I2C Host does not run in standby.
GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE stays on in every sleep mode.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Write 0x5 to make the SERCOM an I2C Host. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the peripheral on or off. The change takes effect after a synchronization delay; the written value reads back at once and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE stays set until the change is done. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every SERCOM register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disables the SERCOM; writing 0 does nothing. It wins over any other write in the same access, which is dropped. Register writes during the reset give an APB error, and reads return reset values. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST clear together when the reset, delayed by synchronization, is done. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: ACKACT
fields.text: What the Host answers after receiving a data byte from the Client. The answer goes out on a write to CTRLB.CMD, or, with smart mode on (CTRLB.SMEN = 1), on a read of DATA.DATA. Not enable-protected, not write-synchronized.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Strobe bits that start a host operation when written; they read back as 0. The acknowledge action applies only when the host is reading; when writing, a command gives only a repeated start or a stop. CTRLB.ACKACT may be written together with CMD, and the new acknowledge action takes effect before the command runs. A command is accepted only while INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB is 1. 0x1 sends a repeated start and then the address held in ADDR.ADDR; to send a different address, write ADDR.ADDR instead of CMD, which gives a repeated start and the new address. A command sets SYNCBUSY.SYSOP. Not enable-protected.

rows: Acknowledge action, then a repeated start.
Acknowledge action, then a byte read.
Acknowledge action, then a stop condition.

fields.name: QCEN
fields.text: Quick Command enable. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SMEN
fields.text: Smart mode: the acknowledge action goes out when DATA.DATA is read. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: HSBAUDLOW
fields.text: SCL low time in High-speed mode when non-zero: HSBAUDLOW = fGCLK x TLOW - 1. When zero, HSBAUD times TLOW and THIGH as well as the setup and hold times TSU;STO, THD;STA, TSU;STA. BAUD always times TBUF.

fields.name: HSBAUD
fields.text: SCL high time in High-speed mode: HSBAUD = fGCLK x THIGH - 1. With HSBAUDLOW at 0 this value also gives TLOW and the setup and hold times TSU;STO, THD;STA, TSU;STA. BAUD times TBUF.

fields.name: BAUDLOW
fields.text: When non-zero, sets the SCL low time from the value written.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Sets the SCL high time when BAUD.BAUDLOW is non-zero; when BAUDLOW is zero it sets both the high and low periods of SCL.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Clears interrupt enables without a read-modify-write; the change also shows in INTENSET.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Error interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Client on Bus interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MB
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Host on Bus interrupt; 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Sets interrupt enables without a read-modify-write; the change also shows in INTENCLR.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Error interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Client on Bus interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MB
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Host on Bus interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Set on any error; each cause has its own STATUS bit: LENERR, SEXTTOUT, MEXTTOUT, LOWTOUT, ARBLOST, BUSERR. Write 1 to clear; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Set when a byte is received in Host read mode without lost arbitration or bus error. While set, the Host holds SCL low, stretching the clock. Writing ADDR.ADDR, writing DATA.DATA, reading DATA.DATA with CTRLB.SMEN on, or writing a valid CTRLB.CMD releases SCL and clears it; writing 1 also clears it. The transfer neither goes on nor ends until one of those actions. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MB
fields.text: Set when a byte is sent in Host write mode, whether or not a bus error or lost arbitration occurred; also set when arbitration is lost while sending a NACK in Host read mode, or on a start condition while the bus state is unknown. While set without lost arbitration, the Host holds SCL low. Writing ADDR.ADDR, writing DATA.DATA, reading DATA.DATA with CTRLB.SMEN on, or writing a valid CTRLB.CMD releases SCL and clears it; writing 1 also clears it. The transfer neither goes on nor ends until one of those actions. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: LENERR
fields.text: Set when a DMA transfer runs with automatic length and the Client NACKs before the Host has written ADDR.LEN bytes. Cleared by writing 1 or by any write to ADDR; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SEXTTOUT
fields.text: Set on a Client SCL low extend time-out. Cleared by any write to ADDR or by writing 1, which normal use does not need; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: MEXTTOUT
fields.text: Set on a Host SCL low time-out. Cleared by writing 1 or by any write to ADDR; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: Set while the Host holds SCL low, stretching the clock; worth reading whenever INTFLAG.SB or MB is 1. Clears once that flag is cleared and a further operation is issued. Writes have no effect. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: LOWTOUT
fields.text: Set on an SCL low time-out. Cleared by writing 1 or by any write to ADDR; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: BUSSTATE
fields.text: Current I2C bus state. From UNKNOWN, writing 0x1 forces IDLE; no other state can be forced. Forcing IDLE sets SYNCBUSY.SYSOP.

values.name: UNKNOWN
values.text: Unknown to the Host; it waits for a stop condition or for software to force idle.

values.name: IDLE
values.text: Idle, waiting for a transaction to start.

fields.name: RXNACK
fields.text: Shows whether the most recent address or data packet sent got an ACK. Writes have no effect. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: ARBLOST
fields.text: Set when arbitration is lost while sending a high data bit or a NACK, or during a start or repeated start the Host issues; INTFLAG.MB sets with it. Cleared by writing ADDR.ADDR or by writing 1; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: BUSERR
fields.text: Set on an illegal bus condition, whoever owns the bus: a start, repeated start or stop that breaks the protocol (a start straight followed by a stop is one), or a time-out during a frame. If this Host owns the bus at the time, STATUS.ARBLOST and INTFLAG.MB are set too. Cleared by writing ADDR.ADDR or by writing 1; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SYSOP
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLB.CMD, STATUS.BUSSTATE, ADDR or DATA, made with the SERCOM enabled, is being synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized. Writes to any register other than CTRLA.SWRST meanwhile are dropped and give an APB error.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized. Writes to any register meanwhile are dropped and give an APB error.

fields.name: LEN
fields.text: Length of a DMA transfer, 0 to 255 bytes. LENEN must be 1 for DMA use.

fields.name: TENBITEN
fields.text: Turns on 10-bit addressing; may be written in the same access as ADDR to mark a 10-bit or 7-bit address.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Turns on high-speed mode for this transfer, lasting from the repeated START until the STOP; may be written in the same access as ADDR.

fields.name: LENEN
fields.text: Transfer length enable.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Writing an address starts an action that depends on STATUS.BUSSTATE. UNKNOWN: MB in INTFLAG and BUSERR in STATUS get set and nothing more happens. BUSY: the Host waits for IDLE. IDLE: the Host sends a start condition and the address; on ACK it holds SCL low and sets STATUS.CLKHOLD and INTFLAG.MB. OWNER: a repeated start follows, preceded by the acknowledge action if the last transfer was a read; this write is made while one of the INTFLAG bits MB or SB is 1. A write clears BUSERR and ARBLOST in STATUS and MB and SB in INTFLAG. Reads never disturb the bus. Bit 0 is the R/W bit: 0 write, 1 read.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Window onto the Host's transmit and receive buffers. Reads and writes succeed only while the Host holds SCL low (STATUS.CLKHOLD = 1), except reading the last byte after the stop has gone out. An access starts bus activity that depends on CTRLB.ACKACT, CTRLB.SMEN and the access direction.

fields.name: DBGSTOP
fields.text: Behaviour while an external debugger halts the CPU.

fields.name: COPENx
fields.text: Bit x picks the capture trigger for channel x: event or I/O pin.

fields.name: CAPTENx
fields.text: Bit x makes channel x a capture channel instead of a compare channel. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ALOCK
fields.text: When set, CTRLB.LUPD is set to 1 on every overflow, underflow or re-trigger event. Not synchronized.

values.text: LUPD goes to 1 at every overflow, underflow or re-trigger event.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Counter prescaler factor. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ONDEMAND
fields.text: Whether a stopped TC keeps asking for its clock. In standby with CTRLA.RUNSTDBY at 0, this bit is forced to 0. Not synchronized.

values.text: Off: the TC keeps requesting the clock while stopped (STATUS.STOP = 1).
On: a stopped TC does not request the clock; it asks again on a software re-trigger command or an event with a start or re-trigger action.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Keeps the TC running in standby. Not synchronized.

fields.name: PRESCSYNC
fields.text: Whether the counter wraps on the next GCLK_TCx edge or on the next prescaled edge, with an option to reset the prescaler. Not synchronized.

values.name: GCLK
values.text: Reload or reset the counter on the next generic clock.

values.name: PRESC
values.text: Reload or reset the counter on the next prescaler clock.

values.name: RESYNC
values.text: Reload or reset the counter on the next generic clock and reset the prescaler.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Counter width. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the peripheral on or off. The change takes effect after a synchronization delay; the written value reads back at once and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE stays set until the change is done. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every TC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disables the TC; writing 0 does nothing. It wins over any other write in the same access, which is dropped. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST clear together when the reset, delayed by synchronization, is done. Not enable-protected.

registers.name: CTRLBCLR
